- Application Method for Damaged Card Replacement: Submitting a request at any branch, sent for issuance attached with the damaged card
- Processing Time for Damaged Card Replacement: From 5–7 working days
- Application Method for Card Blocking (Loss/Theft): Through the call center / through the internet banking application
- Processing Time for Card Blocking (Loss/Theft): Instantly
- Application Method for Card Blocking for Other Reasons (Death, Non-Receipt, etc.): Submitting a request at any branch
- Processing Time for Card Blocking for Other Reasons: One working day
- Method for Removing Card Block (Except Delinquency): Submitting a request at any branch
- Processing Time for Removing Card Block (Except Delinquency): From 3–5 working days
- Method for Removing Card Block Due to Delinquency Over 3 Months: Submitting a request at the issuing branch, sent to collections, i-Score fees must be paid
- Processing Time for Removing Delinquency Block Over 3 Months: 10 working days
- Method for Re-Issuance Due to Non-Receipt: Submitting a request at the issuing branch, sent for issuance
- Processing Time for Re-Issuance Due to Non-Receipt: From 3–5 working days
- Method for Card Cancellation: Submitting a request at any branch / submitting a request through the call center
- Processing Time for Card Cancellation: 10 working days
- Change of Payment Method: Submitting a request at any branch
- Change of Payment Method #2: If the modification to the payment method is changing the automatic deduction from 5% to 100% or vice versa, the modification will apply to the card starting from the month following execution of the request
- Change of Payment Method #3: From account or payroll card to cash deposit on POS, the modification will apply to the card from the same month of submitting the request
- Change of Payment Method #4: In case of modifying the account number or payroll card from which deduction is made, the modification will apply to the card from the same month of submitting the request
- Processing Time for Changing Payment Method: Same working day for requests received before 1 PM and the next day for requests received after 1 PM
- Certificate (from Central Collection Department): Submitting a request at the branch, sent to the Central Collections Department for one of the following reasons…
- Processing Time for Central Collection Certificate: Two working days
- Processing Time for Early Settlement Request: "2 working days in case of installment through the Call Center, 4 working days in case of installment through contracted merchants"
- Refund of Credit Balance: By submitting a request on the CIBEL system from the Call Center side
- Processing Time for Credit Balance Refund: From 3–5 working days
- Card Upgrade and Downgrade (Card Type): "Submit the request from the Call Center or branch"
- Processing Time for Card Upgrade/Downgrade: 8 working days
- Credit Card Data Update: Submit a request at the branch
- Processing Time for Credit Card Data Update: Same working day for requests received before 1:00 PM, and the next day for requests received after 1:00 PM
- Card Issuance Fees (Banque Misr Employees): Banque Misr employees are exempted from issuance, renewal, lost and damaged replacement fees
- Credit Card Cancellation: Through the call center
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions: Receiving the cancellation request from the primary cardholder in case of requesting cancellation of the main or supplementary card, provided that the call is made from the registered phone number
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #2: Customer death
- Credit Card Non-Cancellation Conditions: Existence of any outstanding dues, and the customer is informed of the dues to settle them first
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #3: Informing the customer of the outstanding dues to cancel the card,
Debit transactions (purchases / cash withdrawals)
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #4: Informing the customer of the outstanding dues to cancel the card,
Outstanding future installments, if any (installments via HPS system and/or installments at contracted merchants for primary and supplementary cards)
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #5: In case there are due installments,
Create an expedited payment request for due installments via merchants and inform the client to call back to request cancellation after full payment
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #6: In case there are due installments,
If there are installments for HPS system transactions, expedited payment is executed via the call center as usual
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #7: Informing the customer to retain the card,
Inform the client to retain the card, and it will not be suspended or canceled until the Customer Retention Department contacts them within two business days
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #8: Verifying that there is no outstanding balance on the card, a request is created on the Sibel system
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #9: In case there is a credit balance,
The client’s account number / payroll card number / prepaid card number has been obtained to transfer the credit balance (if the balance is greater than 10 EGP) during the cancellation process.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #10: Customer request to settle the dues from the guarantee,
The client is directed to submit the request at the branch.
- Supplementary Credit Card Cancellation Conditions: Customer’s desire to cancel the supplementary card while there are installments on the Info View system related to the supplementary card,
Perform expedited payment for those installments first, then submit the request for the client after completing the expedited payment.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #11: Existence of installment amounts through the call center,Verify the “Extra Loan” field in the Balance screen.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #12: Existence of suspended interest that will be calculated at the end of the month,
Verify the “Pending Interest” field.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #13: Existence of installments through contracted merchants,
Check the Transaction List screen to see if the installment on the 25th of each month is recorded under the name “Banquemisr Taksit.”
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #14: Existence of installments through contracted merchants,
Check the Info View system to see if there are any ongoing installment transactions.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #15: Informing the customer to follow up on the card balance,
Pay any debit amounts due on the card caused by added charges such as late fees, over-limit fees, proportional stamp duty, renewal fees, or accrued interest recorded on the client.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #16: In case there are credit amounts due to the customer,
If there are no accounts or prepaid cards, the client is directed to issue a prepaid card to transfer the credit amount to it, or explicit consent is obtained from the client to waive the amount in favor of the bank if they do not wish to issue a prepaid card.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #17: The credit card can be canceled before activation, and the customer is not forced to activate it in order to cancel
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #18: Cards can be canceled by the branch for customers who did not attend the branch to receive the card without the branch activating it
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #19: Issuing a final clearance,
A final settlement is issued to the client 30 days after the card is canceled in the system.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #20: The guarantee can be refunded fully or partially after 14 days from the card cancellation date
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #21: If the card is not activated, the hold on the guarantee is released on the same day immediately upon card cancellation
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #22: In case the specified period of 14 days passes and the hold on the guarantee is not released, the card cancellation date on the system is first verified, then a complaint “Delay in releasing hold on guarantee” is submitted

- Application Submission Methods #2: Through internet and mobile banking, the customer will be contacted to explain the procedures through the Telesales department

- Early Settlement #2: A request is created on the Sibel system and sent to the Credit Department for standard credit cards and Master Installment card only for merchant transactions without interest and installment transactions made through the call center

- Application Submission Methods #3: The request is submitted through any standard branch for standard cards
- Required Documents for Issuance: Original issuance request, clear and fully completed
- Required Documents for Issuance #2: Copy of the client’s valid National ID, certified by the branch
- Required Documents for Issuance #3: Undated promissory note, signed by the client and approved for unscured Credit card
- Required Documents for Issuance #4: Authorization to fill the promissory note, signed by the client and approved by the branch for unscured Credit card

- Required Documents for Issuance #6: Local and international lists

- Required Documents for Issuance #9: Original issuance request, clear and fully completed (client signature required with requested card type) If credit card limit exceed 100K
- Note for Credit Card Issuance: Credit cards are issued to foreigners without collateral (i.e., salary statement) provided the employer undertakes to pay the debt
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #2: Primary credit cards with personal guarantee are issued from age 21 to 65
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #3: Primary credit cards with tangible collateral are issued from minimum age 21 with no maximum
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #4: Credit cards with tangible collateral are not issued in foreign currency
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #5: Issued cards (new, renewal, lost, damaged, reissued) are held by the department to deliver to clients via shipping companies for a maximum of three months from issuance, then undelivered cards are destroyed
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #6: لا يوجد حاليا حد اقصى لإصدار بطاقات ائتمانية لعميل واحد ولا يتم اصدار بطاقة ائتمانية من نفس النوع سواء فيزا او ماستر
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #7: Credit cards are granted against savings instruments in Egyptian Pounds
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #8: Card may be issued against savings instruments of the donor or jointly held, subject to Legal Department review case by case
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #9: Card may be issued against savings instruments in the name of others up to fourth-degree relatives; beyond that, consult the relevant departments
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #10: "A credit card may be issued to the natural guardian secured by savings instruments in the minor’s name: the source of funds must be the natural guardian. Upon reaching legal age, the minor signs to validate balances including the frozen savings instrument for the card issued to the guardian"
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #11: For foreign clients, granting is based on lending ratios of each savings instrument, or 80% of collateral, or redemption value, whichever is less
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee: Cards are issued up to 90% of nominal collateral value and not exceeding redemption value for the following accounts: savings, Islamic investment current account (Kenana Plus), deposits, day-to-day account, Talaat Harb Certificate (2), Islamic savings certificates, Summit certificate, triple certificate with variable yield
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #2: Cards are issued up to 90% of nominal collateral value and not exceeding redemption value for the following certificates: 10-year increasing certificates and other certificates
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #3: Other savings instruments according to Credit Department
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #4: Credit card may be issued on accounts with joint CIF number
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #5: Collateral is blocked with card issuance while returns are credited to client account as usual
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #6: Pledge declaration fees are collected by the branch and paid to the real estate registry + 1 EGP stamp duty
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #7: Tangible collateral may be changed at the branch, i.e., block another collateral without cancelling the card upon branch request to Credit Department, e.g., "change credit card collateral from Summit Certificate to Triple Certificate"
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #8: يمكن إصدار البطاقة بضمان أوعية إدخارية باسم الغير و حتي درجة القرابة الرابعة ، و فيما عدا درجات القرابة المذكوره يتم الرجوع للادارات المختصه 
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #9: Collateral is fully released after 14 calendar days from actual card cancellation upon branch request to Card Issuance & Modification Department
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #10: Old collateral is released immediately upon replacing it with a new collateral after referral to Card Issuance & Modification Department to unblock and freeze collateral
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #11: For issued cards not activated, the collateral is fully unblocked immediately upon card cancellation
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #12: If client asks whether I-Score affects credit card issuance with tangible collateral, they are informed it depends on Credit Department discretion
- Personal Guarantee: Private sector employer must be coded with Banque Misr; all public/government entities are already coded
- Personal Guarantee #2: Salary transfer to Banque Misr is not required
- Personal Guarantee #3: Minimum net salary: EGP 1,000 for public sector, EGP 2,000 for private sector
- Personal Guarantee #4: Required documents: salary statement stamped by company and company bank (private sector) or social insurance statement as substitute for bank & company stamp (public sector) + utility bill for same address not older than 3 months + copy of valid National ID
- Personal Guarantee #5: Employer must be coded at Banque Misr

- Armed Forces Personnel Program: Ability to issue all types of credit cards to Armed Forces personnel (civilian and military) whose salaries are transferred to Banque Misr (Account 111) with credit limits up to 4 times the transferred salary, with exemption up to age 70
- Armed Forces Personnel Program #2: Cards may also be issued to Armed Forces employees according to an income proof program only, without salary transfer; in this case, the client is not exempted from issuance fees
- Credit Card Issuance Program Using Virtual Income: Issued to savings account clients at our bank, Egyptians only, without blocking the collateral, provided they are employees or owners of commercial activities and free professions, through calculating a virtual income based on savings rates to determine their virtual income
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program: Client must be a bank customer for at least 12 months before card request and must hold savings instruments
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #2: Client must be regular in repayment of any credit facilities according to the I-Score report
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #3: Minimum virtual income: EGP 10,000 for new issuance
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #4: For joint account clients, all grant conditions apply to each client individually, and net savings are calculated based on each client’s share
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #5: Client age must not be less than 21 and not more than 65
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #6: Client must not have any existing facilities with income proof / pension / salary transfer
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #7: Client’s salary or pension must not be transferred to any account or payroll card
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #8: Employer classification is not required; dealings with suspended companies are allowed
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #9: For clients of free professions/businesses, bankruptcy and protest certificate fees are collected
- Method of Calculating Virtual Income: Client net savings value after excluding savings blocked for other credit facilities (average of last 6 months) / 6.6
- Virtual Income Payment Method: The credit card is linked to the account to pay only the minimum due on the card monthly
- Conversion of Cards Issued Against Savings Instruments into Virtual Income–Based Cards: Convert issued cards secured by savings instruments to virtual income-backed cards for clients requesting cancellation of savings-backed credit cards
- Conversion of Cards Issued Against Savings Instruments into Virtual Income–Based Cards #2: Minimum average savings for clients over 12 months: EGP 500,000
- Conversion of Cards Issued Against Savings Instruments into Virtual Income–Based Cards #3: Client must be regular in repayment according to credit policy
- Conversion of Cards Issued Against Savings Instruments into Virtual Income–Based Cards #4: New grant conditions are applied according to the virtual income program
- Card to Card Program: It is a credit card issuance program through virtual income calculation for clients issued cards without tangible collateral (with personal guarantee) at other banks based on credit limit granted by those banks
- Card to Card Program #2: Credit card issuance program through virtual income calculation for clients issued cards with personal guarantee ("salaries") at other banks based on credit limit granted by those banks
- Card to Card Program Conditions: Client must be Egyptian resident in Egypt, either employees, business owners, or free professions, whose salaries are not transferred
- Card to Card Program Conditions #2: Clients whose salaries are transferred to the bank in specific fields (e.g., doctors, teachers, university professors) or who previously obtained facilities from the bank only
- Card to Card Program Conditions #3: Client must be regular per I-Score report, and digital score must not be less than 500
- Card to Card Program Conditions #4: At least 6 months must have passed since issuance of any client’s primary cards at other banks, and they must be active on the system
- Credit Limit According to i-Score for Card to Card Program: Minimum EGP 20,000 for employees, human doctors, and pharmacists
- Credit Limit According to i-Score for Card to Card Program #2: Minimum EGP 20,000 for business owners and other free professions
- Credit Limit Condition According to i-Score for Card to Card Program: Client usage of the granted card must not be less than 10% of credit limit as usage indicator; calculated based on highest credit - card balance - last payment (whichever is higher per I-Score or client provides statement showing usage)
- Method of Calculating Virtual Income for Card to Card Program: Virtual income represents the highest credit limit of the primary unsecured credit card divided by 2
- Method of Calculating Virtual Income for Card to Card Program #2: Virtual income is compared with virtual income declared by client during desk inquiry; debt burden and credit limit are calculated using the lesser income value
- Proposed Credit Limit for Card to Card Program: Equivalent to 120% of used credit limit in income calculation or maximum based on 50% debt burden, whichever is lower, max EGP 250,000
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks: Issue credit cards through virtual income calculation for clients with unsecured personal loans from other banks for at least 1 year
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #2: Target categories: Egyptian residents in Egypt, private/public/government employees, holding unsecured loans from other banks
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #3: Minimum income: EGP 10,000
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #4: Income multiplier: 200% of calculated virtual income
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #5: Maximum credit limit: EGP 250,000 without violating monthly debt burden ratio
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #6: Minimum age: 21
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #7: Maximum age: 60 for employees (except those in entities with retirement age 65)
- Target Segments for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors: Medical doctors
- Target Segments for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #2: Dentists
- Target Segments for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #3: Physiotherapists
- Target Segments for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #4: Medical doctors owning labs or radiology centers, based on years of experience and start date of activity according to the medical facility license
- Target Segments for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #5: University professors and lecturers according to job grades
- Target Segments for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #6: (Assistant lecturer, teaching assistant, lecturer, assistant professor, professor) whose income is difficult to verify based on grade or job title
- General Granting Conditions for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors: Client must be regular in repayment
- General Granting Conditions for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #2: Client’s data must be updated in the banking system
- General Granting Conditions for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #3: Client cannot combine more than one virtual income program from the following: cash loans, agency Murabaha, credit cards
- General Granting Conditions for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #4: For bank clients with the following jobs: "doctors – teachers – university professors," whose salaries are transferred to us, or clients who previously obtained facilities from us and whose income is recorded in the system, they may be granted under virtual income programs, due to the presence of other income sources besides their main job, which are difficult to verify
- General Granting Conditions for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #5: Conduct field and desk inquiries
- Required Documents for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors: Request for credit card issuance including basic data
- Required Documents for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #2: Sign a promissory note and authorize its completion
- Required Documents for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #3: Valid copy of the national ID card
- Required Documents for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #4: Recent utility bill
- Required Documents for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #5: Client income declaration
- Required Documents for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #6: Include client income in the issuance request
- Required Documents for Egyptian University Doctors and Professors: Job grade is determined by one of the following alternatives:
- Required Documents for Egyptian University Doctors and Professors #2: According to client’s national ID, issued within the last 6 months, showing job grade and employer
- Required Documents for Egyptian University Doctors and Professors #3: According to a recent certified official document showing current job grade
- Required Documents for Egyptian University Doctors and Professors #4: Conduct field inquiry with employer to verify client’s job
- Required Documents – Doctors’ Years of Experience Program: Professional practice license
- Required Documents – Doctors’ Years of Experience Program #2: Valid copy of tax card
- Required Documents – Doctors’ Years of Experience Program #3: Professional association membership card
- Required Documents – Doctors’ Years of Experience Program #4: Clinic or medical center license
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category One): Clients with accounts at our bank / other banks during the last 6 months
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Two): Premium bank clients whose unblocked savings over the last 6 months ranged from EGP 1 million to 2.5 million, provided monthly balance for last 2 months meets this value
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Two) #2: MID CAP bank clients with annual sales of EGP 200 million+, operating for 1+ years, regular in repayment, and company credit rating ORR 5 max
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Two) #3: Clients with accounts at our bank / other banks, monthly cash flow after calculating company share: EGP 4 million – 7.5 million (monthly income EGP 800k – 1.5 million)
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Two) #4: Premium clients with unblocked savings of EGP 2.5 million+ over last 6 months, provided monthly balance for last 2 months meets this value
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Two) #5: Clients with POS transactions at our bank for 1 year, monthly transaction average ≥ EGP 1 million
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Three): Premium clients with unblocked savings over EGP 2.5 million in last 6 months, provided monthly balance for last 2 months meets this value
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Three) #2: Large Corporate clients with annual sales ≥ EGP 200 million, operating ≥1 year, regular in repayment, ORR ≤ 5
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Three) #3: Clients with POS transactions at our bank for 1 year, monthly average ≥ EGP 2 million
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Three) #4: Clients with accounts at our bank / other banks, monthly cash flow after calculating company share > EGP 7.5 million (monthly income > EGP 1.5 million)
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program: Client must be regular in repayment
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #2: Service is not provided to clients requiring data update until procedures are completed
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #3: High-risk clients are referred to the Anti-Financial Crimes Department at Compliance & Institutional Governance Sector
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #4: Reductions and unblocking are done in accordance with governing instructions
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #5: Credit limit increases after 6 months from card issuance or last increase, adhering to income multiplier and category maximum
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #6: Minimum client age: 25
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #7: Maximum client age: 65
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #8: 6 months except for Mid Cap and Large Corporate clients
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #9: Minimum income: EGP 25,000 – 60,000
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #10: Minimum business activity duration: 2 years
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #11: Maximum card limit
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #12: Maximum card limit
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #13: Maximum card limit
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #14: Maximum card limit
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program: Valid copy of national ID
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #2: Recent income proof according to unified credit policy
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #3: Recent utility bill per unified credit policy procedure
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #4: Recent official extract from commercial registry for last 6 months or professional license
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #5: Valid copy of tax card
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #6: Copy of latest amendment to company incorporation to determine partner’s share where required
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #7: Bank statements for last 6 months in client’s or company’s name, or tax certificate showing taxable income for last year
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #8: Commercial judgments certificate (bankruptcy and protest for client/company)
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #9: Returned checks report for client/company for last 2 years per field inquiry or branch report
- Classic Cards Are Not Issued Against Tangible Collateral: Classic cards are not issued with tangible collateral
- Guarantee #2: Savings account, deposit, certificate
- Guarantee #3: With personal guarantee (salary)
- Processing Time for Credit Cards – Secured by Collateral: يوم العمل التالي من استلام الطلب
- Processing Time for Credit Cards – Unsecured: In case of requesting credit card issuance through Telesales, 3 working days for secured credit cards, and if the request is received after 1 PM, 3 working days are counted starting from the next working day
- Processing Time for Credit Cards – Unsecured #2: Submitting the request at branches: 5 working days
- Processing Time for Credit Cards – Unsecured #3: In case of requesting credit card issuance through Telesales: 6 working days
- Credit Limit Increase: The request is submitted through any branch
- Credit Limit Increase #2: The customer must be regular in payment
- Credit Limit Increase #3: Applying for a credit limit increase without a specific time condition in case of cards with tangible or personal guarantee
- Credit Limit Increase #4: Credit inquiry fees must be paid (charged as debt on the card)
- Credit Limit Increase #5: Increasing the credit limit does not result in changing the card type, but if the customer wishes to change the card type, a card upgrade request is made
- Credit Limit Increase #6: The customer’s request is rejected if the customer is listed on negative lists
- Credit Limit Increase #7: A new guarantee or new income statements are submitted in case the amount is insufficient
- Credit Limit Decrease: The request is submitted at any branch
- Credit Limit Decrease #2: The outstanding balance must be settled to less than the limit requested to be reduced
- Credit Limit Decrease #3: The card is suspended as part of the reduction procedure under the name “Decrease limit” and is automatically reactivated after executing the request
- Credit Limit Decrease #4: The difference in the guarantee can be refunded after 14 days from reducing the credit limit without requiring any requests from the customer to release the hold on the guarantee
- Credit Limit Decrease #5: There is no reduction for Gold below 3000 EGP or for Classic below 1000 EGP
- Credit Limit Decrease #6: Reducing the credit limit does not result in changing the card type

- Use of Card: في عمليات الشراء والسحب النقدى محليا ودوليا والسداد بالجنية المصرى 
- Limit Use: إمكانية استخدام 100% من الحد الائتمانى للبطاقة في السحب النقدى

- Payment method #2: BM branches
- Payment method #3: BM Online 
- International usage: available after 2 months for credit cards following their date of issuance
- Use of Funds: Purchases from (merchants / internet) or cash withdrawal
- Use of Funds #2: Using the card credit limit for local purchases more than once monthly in case the customer pays within the month
- Use of Funds #3: Using the card credit limit for cash withdrawal only once per month even if the customer pays during the month and the balance becomes available
- Use of Funds #4: The customer may deposit on the card more than once during the month provided that total deposits do not exceed 130% of the card credit limit, in case the full credit limit is used during the month
- Use of Funds #5: If the customer uses the full card credit limit, an additional 5% of the credit limit value will be available for purchase use only for credit cards, and if this percentage is used, the customer balance will become negative, except for (Classic – Gold – Titanium) cards, without informing the customer that other card types are allowed an additional 5% usage limit
- Use of Funds – Payment Conditions: Settlement of the amounts used from the credit limit until the 26th of the following month
- Issuance fees first and other years: EGP 250
- Issuance fees supplimentary first and other years: 100 جم 
- Renewal

- Application Method for Damaged Card Replacement: Submitting a request at any branch, sent for issuance attached with the damaged card
- Processing Time for Damaged Card Replacement: From 5–7 working days
- Application Method for Card Blocking (Loss/Theft): Through the call center / through the internet banking application
- Processing Time for Card Blocking (Loss/Theft): Instantly
- Application Method for Card Blocking for Other Reasons (Death, Non-Receipt, etc.): Submitting a request at any branch
- Processing Time for Card Blocking for Other Reasons: One working day
- Method for Removing Card Block (Except Delinquency): Submitting a request at any branch
- Processing Time for Removing Card Block (Except Delinquency): From 3–5 working days
- Method for Removing Card Block Due to Delinquency Over 3 Months: Submitting a request at the issuing branch, sent to collections, i-Score fees must be paid
- Processing Time for Removing Delinquency Block Over 3 Months: 10 working days
- Method for Re-Issuance Due to Non-Receipt: Submitting a request at the issuing branch, sent for issuance
- Processing Time for Re-Issuance Due to Non-Receipt: From 3–5 working days
- Method for Card Cancellation: Submitting a request at any branch / submitting a request through the call center
- Processing Time for Card Cancellation: 10 working days
- Change of Payment Method: Submitting a request at any branch
- Change of Payment Method #2: If the modification to the payment method is changing the automatic deduction from 5% to 100% or vice versa, the modification will apply to the card starting from the month following execution of the request
- Change of Payment Method #3: From account or payroll card to cash deposit on POS, the modification will apply to the card from the same month of submitting the request
- Change of Payment Method #4: In case of modifying the account number or payroll card from which deduction is made, the modification will apply to the card from the same month of submitting the request
- Processing Time for Changing Payment Method: Same working day for requests received before 1 PM and the next day for requests received after 1 PM
- Certificate (from Central Collection Department): Submitting a request at the branch, sent to the Central Collections Department for one of the following reasons…
- Processing Time for Central Collection Certificate: Two working days
- Processing Time for Early Settlement Request: "2 working days in case of installment through the Call Center, 4 working days in case of installment through contracted merchants"
- Refund of Credit Balance: By submitting a request on the CIBEL system from the Call Center side
- Processing Time for Credit Balance Refund: From 3–5 working days
- Card Upgrade and Downgrade (Card Type): "Submit the request from the Call Center or branch"
- Processing Time for Card Upgrade/Downgrade: 8 working days
- Credit Card Data Update: Submit a request at the branch
- Processing Time for Credit Card Data Update: Same working day for requests received before 1:00 PM, and the next day for requests received after 1:00 PM
- Card Issuance Fees (Banque Misr Employees): Banque Misr employees are exempted from issuance, renewal, lost and damaged replacement fees
- Credit Card Cancellation: Through the call center
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions: Receiving the cancellation request from the primary cardholder in case of requesting cancellation of the main or supplementary card, provided that the call is made from the registered phone number
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #2: Customer death
- Credit Card Non-Cancellation Conditions: Existence of any outstanding dues, and the customer is informed of the dues to settle them first
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #3: Informing the customer of the outstanding dues to cancel the card,
Debit transactions (purchases / cash withdrawals)
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #4: Informing the customer of the outstanding dues to cancel the card,
Outstanding future installments, if any (installments via HPS system and/or installments at contracted merchants for primary and supplementary cards)
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #5: In case there are due installments,
Create an expedited payment request for due installments via merchants and inform the client to call back to request cancellation after full payment
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #6: In case there are due installments,
If there are installments for HPS system transactions, expedited payment is executed via the call center as usual
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #7: Informing the customer to retain the card,
Inform the client to retain the card, and it will not be suspended or canceled until the Customer Retention Department contacts them within two business days
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #8: Verifying that there is no outstanding balance on the card, a request is created on the Sibel system
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #9: In case there is a credit balance,
The client’s account number / payroll card number / prepaid card number has been obtained to transfer the credit balance (if the balance is greater than 10 EGP) during the cancellation process.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #10: Customer request to settle the dues from the guarantee,
The client is directed to submit the request at the branch.
- Supplementary Credit Card Cancellation Conditions: Customer’s desire to cancel the supplementary card while there are installments on the Info View system related to the supplementary card,
Perform expedited payment for those installments first, then submit the request for the client after completing the expedited payment.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #11: Existence of installment amounts through the call center,Verify the “Extra Loan” field in the Balance screen.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #12: Existence of suspended interest that will be calculated at the end of the month,
Verify the “Pending Interest” field.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #13: Existence of installments through contracted merchants,
Check the Transaction List screen to see if the installment on the 25th of each month is recorded under the name “Banquemisr Taksit.”
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #14: Existence of installments through contracted merchants,
Check the Info View system to see if there are any ongoing installment transactions.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #15: Informing the customer to follow up on the card balance,
Pay any debit amounts due on the card caused by added charges such as late fees, over-limit fees, proportional stamp duty, renewal fees, or accrued interest recorded on the client.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #16: In case there are credit amounts due to the customer,
If there are no accounts or prepaid cards, the client is directed to issue a prepaid card to transfer the credit amount to it, or explicit consent is obtained from the client to waive the amount in favor of the bank if they do not wish to issue a prepaid card.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #17: The credit card can be canceled before activation, and the customer is not forced to activate it in order to cancel
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #18: Cards can be canceled by the branch for customers who did not attend the branch to receive the card without the branch activating it
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #19: Issuing a final clearance,
A final settlement is issued to the client 30 days after the card is canceled in the system.
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #20: The guarantee can be refunded fully or partially after 14 days from the card cancellation date
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #21: If the card is not activated, the hold on the guarantee is released on the same day immediately upon card cancellation
- Credit Card Cancellation Conditions #22: In case the specified period of 14 days passes and the hold on the guarantee is not released, the card cancellation date on the system is first verified, then a complaint “Delay in releasing hold on guarantee” is submitted

- Note for Credit Card Issuance: Credit cards are issued to foreigners without collateral (i.e., salary statement) provided the employer undertakes to pay the debt
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #2: Primary credit cards with personal guarantee are issued from age 21 to 65
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #3: Primary credit cards with tangible collateral are issued from minimum age 21 with no maximum
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #4: Credit cards with tangible collateral are not issued in foreign currency
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #5: Issued cards (new, renewal, lost, damaged, reissued) are held by the department to deliver to clients via shipping companies for a maximum of three months from issuance, then undelivered cards are destroyed
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #6: لا يوجد حاليا حد اقصى لإصدار بطاقات ائتمانية لعميل واحد ولا يتم اصدار بطاقة ائتمانية من نفس النوع سواء فيزا او ماستر
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #7: Credit cards are granted against savings instruments in Egyptian Pounds
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #8: Card may be issued against savings instruments of the donor or jointly held, subject to Legal Department review case by case
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #9: Card may be issued against savings instruments in the name of others up to fourth-degree relatives; beyond that, consult the relevant departments
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #10: "A credit card may be issued to the natural guardian secured by savings instruments in the minor’s name: the source of funds must be the natural guardian. Upon reaching legal age, the minor signs to validate balances including the frozen savings instrument for the card issued to the guardian"
- Note for Credit Card Issuance #11: For foreign clients, granting is based on lending ratios of each savings instrument, or 80% of collateral, or redemption value, whichever is less
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee: Cards are issued up to 90% of nominal collateral value and not exceeding redemption value for the following accounts: savings, Islamic investment current account (Kenana Plus), deposits, day-to-day account, Talaat Harb Certificate (2), Islamic savings certificates, Summit certificate, triple certificate with variable yield
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #2: Cards are issued up to 90% of nominal collateral value and not exceeding redemption value for the following certificates: 10-year increasing certificates and other certificates

- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #4: Credit card may be issued on accounts with joint CIF number
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #5: Collateral is blocked with card issuance while returns are credited to client account as usual
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #6: Pledge declaration fees are collected by the branch and paid to the real estate registry + 1 EGP stamp duty
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #7: Tangible collateral may be changed at the branch, i.e., block another collateral without cancelling the card upon branch request to Credit Department, e.g., "change credit card collateral from Summit Certificate to Triple Certificate"
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #8: يمكن إصدار البطاقة بضمان أوعية إدخارية باسم الغير و حتي درجة القرابة الرابعة ، و فيما عدا درجات القرابة المذكوره يتم الرجوع للادارات المختصه 
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #9: Collateral is fully released after 14 calendar days from actual card cancellation upon branch request to Card Issuance & Modification Department
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #10: Old collateral is released immediately upon replacing it with a new collateral after referral to Card Issuance & Modification Department to unblock and freeze collateral
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #11: For issued cards not activated, the collateral is fully unblocked immediately upon card cancellation
- Tangible (Collateral) Guarantee #12: If client asks whether I-Score affects credit card issuance with tangible collateral, they are informed it depends on Credit Department discretion

- Armed Forces Personnel Program: Ability to issue all types of credit cards to Armed Forces personnel (civilian and military) whose salaries are transferred to Banque Misr (Account 111) with credit limits up to 4 times the transferred salary, with exemption up to age 70
- Armed Forces Personnel Program #2: Cards may also be issued to Armed Forces employees according to an income proof program only, without salary transfer; in this case, the client is not exempted from issuance fees
- Credit Card Issuance Program Using Virtual Income: Issued to savings account clients at our bank, Egyptians only, without blocking the collateral, provided they are employees or owners of commercial activities and free professions, through calculating a virtual income based on savings rates to determine their virtual income
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program: Client must be a bank customer for at least 12 months before card request and must hold savings instruments
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #2: Client must be regular in repayment of any credit facilities according to the I-Score report
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #3: Minimum virtual income: EGP 10,000 for new issuance
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #4: For joint account clients, all grant conditions apply to each client individually, and net savings are calculated based on each client’s share
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #5: Client age must not be less than 21 and not more than 65
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #6: Client must not have any existing facilities with income proof / pension / salary transfer
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #7: Client’s salary or pension must not be transferred to any account or payroll card
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #8: Employer classification is not required; dealings with suspended companies are allowed
- Special Conditions of the Virtual Income Program #9: For clients of free professions/businesses, bankruptcy and protest certificate fees are collected
- Method of Calculating Virtual Income: Client net savings value after excluding savings blocked for other credit facilities (average of last 6 months) / 6.6
- Virtual Income Payment Method: The credit card is linked to the account to pay only the minimum due on the card monthly
- Conversion of Cards Issued Against Savings Instruments into Virtual Income–Based Cards: Convert issued cards secured by savings instruments to virtual income-backed cards for clients requesting cancellation of savings-backed credit cards
- Conversion of Cards Issued Against Savings Instruments into Virtual Income–Based Cards #2: Minimum average savings for clients over 12 months: EGP 500,000
- Conversion of Cards Issued Against Savings Instruments into Virtual Income–Based Cards #3: Client must be regular in repayment according to credit policy
- Conversion of Cards Issued Against Savings Instruments into Virtual Income–Based Cards #4: New grant conditions are applied according to the virtual income program
- Card to Card Program: It is a credit card issuance program through virtual income calculation for clients issued cards without tangible collateral (with personal guarantee) at other banks based on credit limit granted by those banks
- Card to Card Program #2: Credit card issuance program through virtual income calculation for clients issued cards with personal guarantee ("salaries") at other banks based on credit limit granted by those banks
- Card to Card Program Conditions: Client must be Egyptian resident in Egypt, either employees, business owners, or free professions, whose salaries are not transferred
- Card to Card Program Conditions #2: Clients whose salaries are transferred to the bank in specific fields (e.g., doctors, teachers, university professors) or who previously obtained facilities from the bank only
- Card to Card Program Conditions #3: Client must be regular per I-Score report, and digital score must not be less than 500
- Card to Card Program Conditions #4: At least 6 months must have passed since issuance of any client’s primary cards at other banks, and they must be active on the system
- Credit Limit According to i-Score for Card to Card Program: Minimum EGP 20,000 for employees, human doctors, and pharmacists
- Credit Limit According to i-Score for Card to Card Program #2: Minimum EGP 20,000 for business owners and other free professions
- Credit Limit Condition According to i-Score for Card to Card Program: Client usage of the granted card must not be less than 10% of credit limit as usage indicator; calculated based on highest credit - card balance - last payment (whichever is higher per I-Score or client provides statement showing usage)
- Method of Calculating Virtual Income for Card to Card Program: Virtual income represents the highest credit limit of the primary unsecured credit card divided by 2
- Method of Calculating Virtual Income for Card to Card Program #2: Virtual income is compared with virtual income declared by client during desk inquiry; debt burden and credit limit are calculated using the lesser income value
- Proposed Credit Limit for Card to Card Program: Equivalent to 120% of used credit limit in income calculation or maximum based on 50% debt burden, whichever is lower, max EGP 250,000
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks: Issue credit cards through virtual income calculation for clients with unsecured personal loans from other banks for at least 1 year
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #2: Target categories: Egyptian residents in Egypt, private/public/government employees, holding unsecured loans from other banks
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #3: Minimum income: EGP 10,000
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #4: Income multiplier: 200% of calculated virtual income
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #5: Maximum credit limit: EGP 250,000 without violating monthly debt burden ratio
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #6: Minimum age: 21
- Card to Loan Program – Other Banks #7: Maximum age: 60 for employees (except those in entities with retirement age 65)

- Target Segments for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #2: Dentists
- Target Segments for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #3: Physiotherapists
- Target Segments for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #4: Medical doctors owning labs or radiology centers, based on years of experience and start date of activity according to the medical facility license
- Target Segments for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #5: University professors and lecturers according to job grades
- Target Segments for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #6: (Assistant lecturer, teaching assistant, lecturer, assistant professor, professor) whose income is difficult to verify based on grade or job title
- General Granting Conditions for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors: Client must be regular in repayment
- General Granting Conditions for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #2: Client’s data must be updated in the banking system
- General Granting Conditions for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #3: Client cannot combine more than one virtual income program from the following: cash loans, agency Murabaha, credit cards
- General Granting Conditions for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #4: For bank clients with the following jobs: "doctors – teachers – university professors," whose salaries are transferred to us, or clients who previously obtained facilities from us and whose income is recorded in the system, they may be granted under virtual income programs, due to the presence of other income sources besides their main job, which are difficult to verify
- General Granting Conditions for the Virtual Income Program for Doctors and Egyptian University Professors #5: Conduct field and desk inquiries

- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category One): Clients with accounts at our bank / other banks during the last 6 months
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Two): Premium bank clients whose unblocked savings over the last 6 months ranged from EGP 1 million to 2.5 million, provided monthly balance for last 2 months meets this value
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Two) #2: MID CAP bank clients with annual sales of EGP 200 million+, operating for 1+ years, regular in repayment, and company credit rating ORR 5 max
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Two) #3: Clients with accounts at our bank / other banks, monthly cash flow after calculating company share: EGP 4 million – 7.5 million (monthly income EGP 800k – 1.5 million)
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Two) #4: Premium clients with unblocked savings of EGP 2.5 million+ over last 6 months, provided monthly balance for last 2 months meets this value
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Two) #5: Clients with POS transactions at our bank for 1 year, monthly transaction average ≥ EGP 1 million
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Three): Premium clients with unblocked savings over EGP 2.5 million in last 6 months, provided monthly balance for last 2 months meets this value
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Three) #2: Large Corporate clients with annual sales ≥ EGP 200 million, operating ≥1 year, regular in repayment, ORR ≤ 5
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Three) #3: Clients with POS transactions at our bank for 1 year, monthly average ≥ EGP 2 million
- Target Segments – Self-Employed Professionals Program (Category Three) #4: Clients with accounts at our bank / other banks, monthly cash flow after calculating company share > EGP 7.5 million (monthly income > EGP 1.5 million)
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program: Client must be regular in repayment
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #2: Service is not provided to clients requiring data update until procedures are completed
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #3: High-risk clients are referred to the Anti-Financial Crimes Department at Compliance & Institutional Governance Sector
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #4: Reductions and unblocking are done in accordance with governing instructions
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #5: Credit limit increases after 6 months from card issuance or last increase, adhering to income multiplier and category maximum
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #6: Minimum client age: 25
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #7: Maximum client age: 65
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #8: 6 months except for Mid Cap and Large Corporate clients
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #9: Minimum income: EGP 25,000 – 60,000
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #10: Minimum business activity duration: 2 years
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #11: Maximum card limit
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #12: Maximum card limit
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #13: Maximum card limit
- General Granting Conditions for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #14: Maximum card limit
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program: Valid copy of national ID
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #2: Recent income proof according to unified credit policy
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #3: Recent utility bill per unified credit policy procedure
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #4: Recent official extract from commercial registry for last 6 months or professional license
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #5: Valid copy of tax card
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #6: Copy of latest amendment to company incorporation to determine partner’s share where required
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #7: Bank statements for last 6 months in client’s or company’s name, or tax certificate showing taxable income for last year
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #8: Commercial judgments certificate (bankruptcy and protest for client/company)
- Required Documents for the Self-Employed Professionals Program #9: Returned checks report for client/company for last 2 years per field inquiry or branch report
- Classic Cards Are Not Issued Against Tangible Collateral: Classic cards are not issued with tangible collateral
- Guarantee #2: Savings account, deposit, certificate
- Guarantee #3: With personal guarantee (salary)
- Processing Time for Credit Cards – Secured by Collateral: يوم العمل التالي من استلام الطلب
- Processing Time for Credit Cards – Unsecured: In case of requesting credit card issuance through Telesales, 3 working days for secured credit cards, and if the request is received after 1 PM, 3 working days are counted starting from the next working day
- Processing Time for Credit Cards – Unsecured #2: Submitting the request at branches: 5 working days
- Processing Time for Credit Cards – Unsecured #3: In case of requesting credit card issuance through Telesales: 6 working days
- Credit Limit Increase: The request is submitted through any branch
- Credit Limit Increase #2: The customer must be regular in payment
- Credit Limit Increase #3: Applying for a credit limit increase without a specific time condition in case of cards with tangible or personal guarantee
- Credit Limit Increase #4: Credit inquiry fees must be paid (charged as debt on the card)
- Credit Limit Increase #5: Increasing the credit limit does not result in changing the card type, but if the customer wishes to change the card type, a card upgrade request is made
- Credit Limit Increase #6: The customer’s request is rejected if the customer is listed on negative lists
- Credit Limit Increase #7: A new guarantee or new income statements are submitted in case the amount is insufficient
- Credit Limit Decrease: The request is submitted at any branch
- Credit Limit Decrease #2: The outstanding balance must be settled to less than the limit requested to be reduced
- Credit Limit Decrease #3: The card is suspended as part of the reduction procedure under the name “Decrease limit” and is automatically reactivated after executing the request
- Credit Limit Decrease #4: The difference in the guarantee can be refunded after 14 days from reducing the credit limit without requiring any requests from the customer to release the hold on the guarantee
- Credit Limit Decrease #5: There is no reduction for Gold below 3000 EGP or for Classic below 1000 EGP
- Credit Limit Decrease #6: Reducing the credit limit does not result in changing the card type
